raw_text:
- overtraining hamstrings (trailrunning 10-25km/w, swimming 1km/week sessions, biking 10-50km/w)
  - I started trailrunning and swimming pretty abruptly. Swimming 0 km and then 1km in each swimming session
- carried cca 10kg downhill & got pain in my right knee (difficulty walking)
- got the bandage & kept doing lighter sport (via ferrata, walking, bouldering), the left knee & hamstrings started to hurt
- Hausartzt tells me it’s overtrained and I should relax it and not do anything, take ibuprofen

- (8-9/2024) 1,5 month not moving almost at all (only in the appartment). Icing, raising knees & hamstrings
  - noticeable muscle knots in the back of thighs - hamstrings?
- (9-10/2024) 1 month walking 5k steps/day, biking 15 km/w, some other weekend activities that require more movement. Sauna helped.

- (15.10.2024) status: both knees hurt, especially when wearing heavy shoes. Tightness in hamstrings, after walking cca 10 km cannot walk further, pain when knee twisted, pain at night and pain sometimes in the morning, sleep <6hrs/day (not because of pain)
  - orthopede makes x ray, which doesn’t show anything. After observation of my legs & knees says, that my right leg has loose bands and moves sideways. Prescribes me a bandage and says that if I still have pain in 2025, I should come by again

- (11-12/2024) physiotherapist who works with triathletes tells me I have flat feet and that is what is causing my knee pain. I start doing exercises to strengthen my feet arches
  - I’ve noticed that whenever I load my thighs with any medium-higher load (15kg, higher bike gears uphill), my knee hurts on top of the knee

- (1/2025) talked to a specialized shop for orthopedic shoe inlays where they do a 3D scan of your feet. He told me I have legs to O and that I should get shoe inlays that correct that, on top of the flat feet. He’s currently preparing me these. He gave me a paper about it, but I unfortunately forgot it at home.

- (22.01.2025) right knee hurts more, left hurts as well. The pain is usually localized on top of my knee or behind the knee
  - especially after loading the knee with weight, running. Never during the movement.
  - it feels like bones grinding against each other, or just long intense pain. Sometimes also lower intensity of pain during longer time
  - started swimming again, but not too much this time, and with better form, and it’s surprisingly not painful
  - doing exercises for improving of the foot arch
- My current questions:
  - what can be the cause of my knee pain? Is it just overtraining or is it caused by some structural issue of my legs ? (flat feet/having legs to O?)
  - Would physiotherapy help me?
  - Would shoe inlays help me?
  - Shoe-wise, my plan is to switch between cushioned light shoes with orthopedic inlays in order to get some relief & barefoot shoes to build up the foot arch, is this the best course of action?
  - Is it okay to very slowly start swimming?
  - Can I improve this by some specific nutrition?
  - What can I do?
  - What should I not do?
  - What time-frame should I be thinking of before returning back to more serious training?
  - Should I be training when I experience pain?

- (22.01.2025) MVZ Oberstdorf:
  - suspicion of innere meniscus leason (Innenmeniskusläsion rechts)
  - Dr proposes MRT
